definition: Black in AI, formally called the Black in AI Workshop, is a technology research organization and affinity group, founded by computer scientists Timnit Gebru and Rediet Abebe in 2017.
details: It started as a conference workshop, later pivoting into an organization. Black in AI increases the presence and inclusion of Black people in the field of artificial intelligence (AI) by creating space for sharing ideas, fostering collaborations, mentorship, and advocacy.

explainer.lead: Black in AI is a technology research organization and affinity group that supports the presence and inclusion of Black people in artificial intelligence. It creates opportunities to share research, form collaborations, receive mentorship, and take part in advocacy.

tiers.eli5: Imagine a club where students who might otherwise feel left out can show their ideas, meet helpful mentors, and work together. Black in AI does something similar for Black people working with computers that can learn and solve problems. It began as a workshop and grew into a wider organization.
tiers.practitioner: An engineer or researcher might participate to present work, discuss ideas, meet collaborators, or seek and offer mentorship. It is a research community rather than a software library, model, or engineering method, so participation should not be confused with adopting a particular technical toolkit.
tiers.paperLevel: Black in AI, formally the Black in AI Workshop, is a technology research organization and affinity group founded by computer scientists Timnit Gebru and Rediet Abebe in 2017. Its stated scope is increasing the presence and inclusion of Black people in AI through idea sharing, collaboration, mentorship, and advocacy. It defines no algorithm, model architecture, or evaluation metric.

explainer.example: A Black graduate student could present early AI research at a Black in AI workshop, receive feedback from other researchers, and meet a mentor or collaborator who helps develop the work further.
